title: Inverse trigonometric values and trigonometric equations on an interval
intro: No calculator. Give exact values, use radians, and show the work for each part. Only real solutions are asked for.

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of cos−1⁡(sin⁡7π6)\cos^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}\right).

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, with the inner value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{7\pi}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{7\pi}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> is the angle in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math> with cosine <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Solve tan−1⁡(2x−1)=π4\tan^{-1}(2x - 1) = \frac{\pi}{4} for xx.
parts.sample: Apply tangent to both sides: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x - 1 = \tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Solve sin⁡(2x)=−32\sin(2x) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} for 0≤x≤π0 \le x \le \pi. Show the work that leads to your answers.

rubric.point: Works with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math> on the doubled interval <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 2\pi]</annotation></semantics></math> and finds <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x = \frac{4\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x = \frac{5\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> (or one correct value of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>)

Both solutions <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, and no others

parts.sample: Let <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = 2x</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le x \le \pi</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le u \le 2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin u = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in Quadrants III and IV with reference angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = \frac{4\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = \frac{5\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Solve 2sin2⁡x+sin⁡x−1=02\sin^2 x + \sin x - 1 = 0 for 0≤x<2π0 \le x < 2\pi. Show the work that leads to your answers.

rubric.point: Factors (or uses the quadratic formula) to get <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = -1</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2\sin x - 1)(\sin x + 1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: All three solutions <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and no others

parts.sample: Treat <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math> as the variable: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2\sin x - 1)(\sin x + 1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, giving <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, giving <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{3\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The solutions are <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
